scenes.heading: What is a Database?
scenes.subheading: An organized system for storing and retrieving data
scenes.narration: A database is an organized collection of data managed by software that lets you store, retrieve, and update information reliably.

scenes.heading: What a database provides
bullets: Fast retrieval through queries and indexes
Concurrent access for many users at once
scenes.narration: A database provides persistent storage, so your data survives restarts and crashes. It enables fast retrieval through queries and indexes, so you find records quickly. It enforces rules that keep the data consistent and valid. And it manages concurrent access, letting many users read and write safely at the same time.

scenes.heading: How you interact with a database
scenes.narration: You interact with a database by sending it a query describing what you want. The database engine plans how to execute that request efficiently. It then reads or writes the underlying data and returns a result to you.

scenes.heading: Files vs a database
scenes.narration: Storing data in plain files gives you no enforced structure and makes updates manual and error-prone. A database imposes structure, validates data, and coordinates concurrent updates safely. It also offers powerful querying that raw files simply cannot match.

scenes.text: A database is the reliable, queryable foundation that keeps data consistent and accessible to many users.
scenes.narration: In essence, a database is the reliable and queryable foundation that keeps data consistent and accessible even under heavy concurrent use.
